title: Evaluating Generate, Validate, and Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate–validate–repair pipeline with a canary stage on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was reused by both conditions; downstream validator/repair was the only mechanism for paired differences. Results: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) did not reach α=0.05 (p = 0.0625). A preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred; model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We reconcile the apparent test/CI discordance by reporting the exact test as the preregistered confirmatory result and characterizing the bootstrap interval as a secondary descriptive summary driven by extremely sparse discordant counts. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, validator traces, and analysis artifacts in the archived run bundle and discuss construct validity and limitations of the shared_initial_candidate comparison.

sections.introduction: Automating intent‑to‑configuration translation for NetOps can reduce operator burden but risks introducing multi‑device policy and sequence violations: LLM outputs may be syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect in workflows requiring ordered actions and protected fields. Prior work documents LLM hallucination and prompt sensitivity for structured outputs and motivates verifier‑assisted pipelines. We ask: in a controlled synthetic workflow corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics, how much does a guarded generate–validate–repair pipeline with a canary stage increase paired safe‑deploy rates relative to a baseline single‑shot LLM generator? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired experimental design emphasizing workflow outcomes; (2) an autonomous execution and analysis run with archived manifests and validator traces; (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation showing a small absolute guarded benefit when baseline validity is already high and repairs are rare.
sections.related_work: Empirical and survey studies document hallucination and high prompt sensitivity in LLMs that affect structured outputs and code/config generation [1]. Methods that enforce schema or constrained decoding increase the rate of executable outputs in structured domains, though much evidence comes from non‑NetOps domains [2,3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system papers demonstrate verifier‑assisted repair and agentic architectures that improve correctness in prototype settings but emphasize dependence on validator fidelity, governance, and audit traces [4,5]. Several proposals advocate protocol‑mediated execution and proof‑carrying traces to close TOCTOU and evidence‑safety gaps; production‑scale validation of these governance layers remains limited [6]. Our study measures an end‑to‑end guarded pipeline against a paired baseline using shared_initial_candidate semantics and a deterministic validator so that downstream validation/repair effects are isolated.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study was preregistered as cand-003-stud-001 and frozen prior to any model calls. Design: paired binary design with 1000 deterministic tasks from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; each task produced exactly one sampled initial generation deterministically reused by both conditions (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). Model scope: declared model gpt-5-mini (provider openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Under the shared_initial_candidate semantics the only mechanism for a paired outcome change is downstream validation and any permitted rescue (repair/canary) executed under the guarded arm. Validator and repair: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital‑twin emulator) performed intent‑constraint validation (presence and ordering of required commands, protected‑field noninterference, workflow policies). When validation failed the guarded pipeline could invoke a single preregistered, validator‑guided repair attempt (maximum one repair call per task). Analysis and statistical procedures: the preregistered primary inferential procedure is the exact two‑sided McNemar paired test on the 2×2 contingency of paired safe‑deploy outcomes (primary hypothesis H1 = guarded > baseline in paired success rate). As a preregistered secondary descriptive summary we computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and reported bootstrap diagnostics. Missingness, multiplicity adjustments (Holm–Bonferroni for secondary claims), stopping rules, and contamination checks were preregistered and followed; no post‑preregistration deviations occurred. Deterministic accounting and execution artifacts are archived.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: start 2026‑09‑01 06:31:07 UTC; completion 2026‑09‑01 08:38:57 UTC. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; failed episodes = 0. Model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial_generation = 1000; repair = 5). Paired contingency (from archived analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 995, n10 = 5, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline successes = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded successes = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (guarded − baseline). Preregistered primary inferential result (exact two‑sided McNemar on the archived contingency): p = 0.0625 (H1 not supported at two‑sided α = 0.05). Preregistered secondary descriptive summary (archived analysis/analysis_log.jsonl shows bootstrap_seed = 1729 and bootstrap_resamples = 10000): paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.001, 0.01]. No preregistered exclusions or contamination flags were triggered. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred under the allowed repair budget.
sections.discussion: Statistical reconciliation and interpretation: the preregistered confirmatory test is the exact two‑sided McNemar test and its p = 0.0625 is the primary result. The bootstrap percentile CI is a preregistered secondary descriptive summary; it should not be interpreted as overturning the preregistered exact test. The apparent discordance stems from extremely sparse discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0): exact conditional tests condition on total discordants and compute tail probabilities of observing at least the observed imbalance, while nonparametric bootstrap percentile intervals approximate the sampling distribution of the paired difference and can yield intervals excluding zero when few discordants dominate the resamples. The archived artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) record the contingency and bootstrap parameters used. Mechanistic insight: under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded arm could change outcomes only via validator‑triggered repair (or canary/rollback); with only five repairs invoked, the observed absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points) is mechanistically attributable to a small number of validator interventions. Operational implication (bounded): verifier‑guided safeguards can avert some unsafe outcomes, but measurable marginal gains depend critically on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, repair budget, and task distribution. Threats to validity: single‑model scope, synthetic corpus and deterministic validator, constrained repair budget, and shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolate downstream effects but do not capture variability from independent first‑pass generations.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired study the guarded generate–validate–repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) over a baseline single‑shot LLM generator on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps corpus; the preregistered exact McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs occurred, and model calls used = 1005. We report the exact test as the preregistered confirmatory outcome and the bootstrap CI as a secondary descriptive summary (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). These results show that downstream verifier/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in workflow settings but that measurable marginal gains can be limited when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when shared_initial_candidate semantics constrain sources of paired variance. We publish preregistration, execution manifests, validator traces, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and encourage follow‑up studies that expand model diversity, validator fidelity, repair budgets, and more realistic multi‑vendor topologies to map NetOps risk–utility tradeoffs of agentic safeguards.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt-5-mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations under alternative prompting or constrained‑generation arms that were not executed.

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5% limited statistical power to detect large absolute improvements; only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining interpretability of repair efficacy.

Statistical nuance: exact McNemar p = 0.0625 (not <0.05) while the executor's bootstrap percentile CI returned [0.001,0.01]; sparse discordant counts and test choice yield sensitivity to analysis method—interpretation must consider both outcomes.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's specification; semantic/policy correctness across multi‑device emergent properties may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled rule set.
